common: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one standalone landscape illustration for a Korean medieval bedtime story learning game, 3:2 ratio, no text, no borders, no collage. Use the supplied approved image as the primary STYLE reference: extremely restrained pale watercolor and gouache, fine illustrative dry-brush on ivory paper, subtle ink/graphite detail; misty gray-blue distant ridges, warm pale limestone, desaturated sage/olive and straw grasses, clouded pearl sky, quiet warm diffused light. Dreamy, nostalgic, spacious and emotionally secure yet narratively legible. Preserve the sophistication and delicate handmade texture of that reference, not cartoon, not photorealistic or shiny 3D. Avoid bright saturated blues/oranges, glossy digital effects, giant swirls, excessive contrast. Consistent characters across the book: knight is an ordinary unglamorous ADULT MAN about 30 with slightly slim wiry build (not muscular, not pretty), short messy muted chestnut hair, weathered plain face, faded olive cloak, worn modest steel/chainmail over beige tunic, leather boots; his shield is RECTANGULAR WOODEN PLANKS with visible grain and a little faded muted blue-green paint, never round. Adviser, when present, is a modest plainly dressed elderly MAN with gray beard. Dragon, when present, is a large original ash gray-brown winged creature with tactile overlapping scales, small cracks, leathery creases on its wings, ridged horns, but painted delicately in pale tones. No gore. No resemblance to a named copyrighted fantasy character.
scenes: SCENE 1 — The blocked road: a large stone bridge leads across a river toward a distant hilltop medieval walled kingdom. The formidable gray dragon lies across the far end of the bridge, wings loosely folded, head slightly raised and one wary eye open; it is an obstacle and enemy. The slim male knight is small in the left foreground seen three quarters from behind, standing cautiously beside a low stone wall, holding his rectangular plank shield and spear. Keep a considerable clear distance between knight and dragon. Do not show a relaxed friendly conversation or confrontation at arm's length. The meandering cobbled path and pale misty valley occupy much of the composition, framing branches and pale spring blossom like the reference.

SCENE 2 — News of tomorrow's battle: ordinary medieval villagers, women and men in muted beige/olive clothes, gather at a stone gateway beneath a soft lantern to read a parchment notice pinned to a timber board. The parchment has a small dragon silhouette and abstract marks, NO legible writing. Faces show quiet concern and attention, not terror. The slim adult male knight with his rectangular wooden shield stands nearby listening. Beyond the arch, glimpse a misty valley and distant stone bridge. A grounded narrative tableau with space, pale paper and delicate ochre light.

SCENE 3 — Objection in the council: inside a humble medieval stone council chamber, two plain middle-aged male council members sit at a rough wooden table, one lifting an open palm in objection, the other shaking his head with worry. Across from them stands the slightly slim ordinary adult male knight, short tousled chestnut hair, olive cloak, quiet serious expression; rectangular wood-plank shield rests against his leg. Quill and rolled papers on table, pale window light, quiet gray limestone arch. Desaturated warm grays and oatmeal, subtle ink facial expressions. No modern suits or microphones.

SCENE 4 — The grandfather's recommendation: in the same modest medieval chamber, a plain elderly male adviser with gray beard and simple brown wool robe steps forward, gesturing openly toward the slim adult male knight beside him as he recommends him to the council. The grandfather's face is wise, warm and unshowy. Knight has short tousled chestnut hair, plain face, worn modest armor and faded olive cloak, a rectangular wooden plank shield in hand. A few attentive council figures and a softly lit arched window in background. Quiet trust and a readable social interaction, pale medieval watercolor, no glamor.

SCENE 5 — A small missing scale: the slim adult male knight crouches hidden behind a broken low stone wall in the near foreground, peering cautiously toward the hostile dragon several body-lengths away on the bridge. His rectangular wood-plank shield is tucked by his side, spear lowered and ready. The dragon is unaware of him, torso angled enough to reveal a single small missing scale on the chest, an uninjured pale patch subtly distinct among textured gray scales. Do not enlarge this patch, no wound or blood, no diagram. Cold gray mist, pale stone and quiet sage vegetation; taut careful observation at distance, never friendly close eye contact.

SCENE 6 — A precise brave throw: a dynamic but restrained medieval watercolor narrative frame. Left foreground the slim male knight is shown just after releasing a wooden spear with his right arm extended, rectangular plank shield held in left arm. The spear travels in a clear line toward the small scale gap on the chest of the large hostile gray dragon at far side of stone bridge. Dragon recoils and lowers its head, beginning surrender. Clearly separate opposing figures and clear arc of action, no blood, no injury detail, no violent close-up. Dry-brush marks lightly suggest motion. Pale muted landscape, cool misty sky.

SCENE 7 — The morning gathering: medieval press conference interpreted as scribes reporting the news. In a pale stone courtyard the slightly slim plain-faced adult male knight stands modestly before a small group of scribes with quills, parchment and simple writing boards, with townspeople listening behind them. The knight gives a shy small wave, his rectangular wooden plank shield rests beside him; elderly male adviser looks quietly proud. Morning pearl light, cream stone, restrained sage and ochre garments, no microphones or modern technology, no readable text. A warm but unshowy resolution.

SCENE 8 — The dragon becomes public transport: the same large ash-gray textured dragon now friendly after surrender flies gently above the misty river valley toward the distant hill kingdom. Several small villagers are seated safely in a modest broad wooden passenger saddle with a protective rail and woven straps along its back; it looks like a practical fantasy public transport service, not a modern vehicle. A small stone landing terrace with a few waiting travelers shows its shared role. Dragon wings spread naturally, clear anatomy, subtle leathery creases and scales. Gentle pale warm evening light, ivory cloud and gray-blue mountains, comforting homeward ending, no bright neon sunset, no text.
